task.name: Routing excludes unavailable models and stops a phase before spend when no model remains
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2949
---

## What

Slice 2 of 3 from the decomposition of #2914. Consumes the availability answers defined in #2949 and threads them into assignment and preflight: unavailable models are excluded from every candidate pool with a logged reason, unverified ones stay eligible with a one-time warning, and a phase left with nothing available or unverified stops the run before any spend. Post-dispatch quarantine is the third slice, not this one.

## Why

Knowing a model is unavailable is worthless unless the router acts on it before the money goes. In the 2026-09-04 incident the refusal arrived after WORKSPACE, preflight, routing and plan had been charged; four stories produced nothing. The availability answer now exists (#2949); this slice is where it changes what gets dispatched. See #2914.

## Acceptance criteria

- A model resolved **unavailable** appears in no phase's candidate pool. Its exclusion is recorded in the routing decision with a canonical reason naming the auth mode and the time of the availability answer, in the same place and shape other exclusions (self-review, taint) are recorded today.
- A model resolved **unverified** remains fully eligible, and the run warns exactly once per model that its availability is unconfirmed. Routing among unverified models is identical to routing today; nothing degrades for a provider that publishes no catalog.
- A phase left with no available or unverified model stops the run before any spend on that story, naming every excluded model and its reason. The stop is a routing outcome, not an agent failure, and is never recorded against any model's capability history.
- Exclusion is applied at the moment of selection from the current availability answer, so an answer that changes between stories in one sprint changes routing for later stories without a restart.

## Example

```
$ forge sprint --issues 2775 ...
  ⚠ ROUTING  openai/gpt-5.4/cli excluded — not available to this account under
             codex ChatGPT-account auth (account catalog, checked 2026-09-05)
  ▸ DEV   gpt-5.4-mini  iter=1
  ✓ DEV   $0.42  4m 11s
```

And where nothing remains:

```
  ✗ ROUTING  no model available for phase dev: openai/gpt-5.4/cli excluded
             (not available to this account), openai/gpt-5.5/cli excluded
             (not available to this account). Nothing dispatched, $0.00 spent.
```

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixes all eight P1 findings and the three P2s that restated them. Two structural changes carry most of it. First, availability is keyed by dispatch identity (provider, transport kind, runner, endpoint) via a new dispatch_key(), not by model name: PhaseUnavailable.excluded, the launch gate's candidate accounting (unavailable_candidates returns excluded-by-identity plus a distinct-candidate count from one derivation), and the router's answers all count identities, so two candidates sharing a model string under different credentials or endpoints are two candidates and a fully-unavailable phase can no longer read as having a survivor. Second, the story resolves ONE StoryAvailability before its first paid call: _run_preflight_phase resolves it and stashes it on CoordinatorState.model_availability, and _apply_preflight_config reuses it (story_availability_for) rather than resolving a second answer that could contradict the phase that already ran. That closes the AC3 gap — preflight runs ahead of routing, so it is now gated on what it actually dispatches (the configured preflight profile and its fallback, via preflight_dispatch_profiles), reseating onto an available fallback or stopping before any invocation. Static routing (adaptive disabled) now honours availability by refusing a configured phase profile the account cannot invoke, instead of returning before the answer was consulted. Explicit reviewer pools are filtered as whole pools before being spliced back AND the runtime review_pool/plan_agent_review pool is rewritten to the filtered list, so an unavailable non-leading reviewer is neither dispatched nor recorded as included. Refusal payloads are built by _pool_exhaustion_payload from the whole pool, naming every candidate with the rule that removed it (availability, capability record, or dev declaration) — the dev-declaration filter moved ahead of the refusal loop so a jointly-emptied dev pool reports both causes. The fixed '$0.00 spent' sentence left the exception for routing_stop_message(exc, spent_usd), supplied by each catching site. AvailabilityWarnings is run-scoped (run_key, reset at sprint launch, run_warning_key derives sprint-or-run) and lock-guarded for the ThreadPoolExecutor workers. The sprint scheduler gained a routing-stop branch: SKIPPED not FAILED, sprint halted, remaining stories skipped pre-dispatch. Found while auditing: restore_routing_decision (resume-without-cache in engine.py) re-derives routing and reached the same gate — it now returns the same RoutingStopped result as the other three call sites.

findings.description: When a multi-profile explicit review_pool or plan_agent_review contains an unavailable reviewer after an available first entry, the coordinator restores that reviewer into the runtime reviewer list and records it in the routing decision as included: true with reason none.
When a sprint phase has two distinct candidates with the same profile.model and both resolve unavailable, check_sprint_availability collapses them to one excluded entry and returns no stop.

After the singleton availability-warning tracker has warned for an unverified model, a later sprint or task run in the same process does not warn for that model because no run-boundary code resets the tracker.

On the live coordinator path the preflight agent runs and is charged (preflight_flow.py:534) before availability is resolved and routing is applied (preflight_flow.py:1140), so a NoAvailableModelError raised there stops the story after preflight spend while its operator-facing message asserts 'Nothing dispatched, $0.00 spent'.

When a role pool empties from the combination of capability exclusions and availability exclusions, the whole-pool guard raises NoAvailableModelError naming only the availability-excluded agents, so the stop message can attribute the emptiness entirely to account availability while capability records removed the other candidates.

check_sprint_availability keys its excluded map by model name while phase_keys is per profile, so a phase whose candidate list contains two profiles sharing one model name never satisfies the equal-length check and the launch gate silently passes even when every candidate is unavailable, deferring the stop to the router.

AVAILABILITY_WARNINGS is a process-wide singleton with a reset() method that no production code calls, so in a process that runs more than one sprint the once-per-run warning is actually once per process and a later sprint's unverified models are silently unannounced.
When adaptive assignment is disabled, story configuration returns before availability is resolved, so unavailable fixed profiles remain dispatchable and unverified profiles emit no warning.

When an explicit review or plan-review pool contains multiple profiles, every profile is restored after filtered assignment and rebuilt as included, so an unavailable non-leading reviewer is dispatched.

In adaptive runs the current availability answer is fetched only after the preflight agent call, while the sprint launch check admits preflight when any adaptive agent is available, so an unavailable configured preflight model can incur cost before routing excludes it.
When a per-story routing stop occurs after sprint launch, the sprint records the infrastructure-flagged PREFLIGHT result as FAILED and continues scheduling instead of stopping the run.
Runs handled by the same Python process share the process-wide warned set, so a later run emits no unverified warning for a model warned about in an earlier run.
When availability and another hard eligibility rule jointly empty a phase, the routing stop names only availability-excluded models and omits every model excluded for the other reason.

When two unavailable phase profiles use the same model string under different credentials or endpoints, the exclusion dictionary collapses them into one entry and the length comparison incorrectly allows the sprint to launch.

findings.description: When an explicit code-review or plan-review pool has an unavailable first reviewer and an available later reviewer, the sprint availability gate reports the phase as having no available model and aborts launch.

When a non-leading explicit reviewer is dropped for unavailability, the runtime review pool is filtered but the routing decision omits that pinned reviewer or records the matching agent only as explicit_override_locked instead of model_unavailable.
When a fixed-profile phase has two unavailable dispatch identities with the same model string, the per-story routing stop collapses them into one excluded entry and names the model only once.

In the preflight-profile refusal catch, state.error is set to the bare exception text while the returned CoordinatorResult message is built via routing_stop_message with the spend tail, so the persisted state error and the operator-facing message for the same stop carry different sentences.

_fixed_profile_availability keys the warning map by profile.model via setdefault, so two configured phase profiles sharing a model string under different endpoints or transports collapse into one warning entry and only the first identity's unverified or unavailable answer is announced.

The resume-path catch around restore_routing_decision converts a NoAvailableModelError into a RoutingStopped result, but no test drives restore_routing_decision to actually raise on a resumed story whose pool emptied, so that conversion is exercised only by inspection.
With adaptive assignment disabled, a review or plan-review pool containing both an available profile and an unavailable profile returns unchanged, so the unavailable reviewer remains dispatchable.

When the first member of an explicit reviewer pool is unavailable but a later member is available, the sprint launch gate examines only the first member and aborts the sprint despite the surviving reviewer.

After an unavailable member is removed from an explicit reviewer pool, the reconciled routing decision omits that profile or labels a matching adaptive agent explicit_override_locked instead of recording model_unavailable with its auth mode and timestamp.
When one unverified dispatch identity appears as a fixed profile and as an agent with a different name, the same run emits separate warnings under the model name and agent name.
When two fixed profiles share a model string across different endpoints and both are unavailable for different reasons, the routing stop contains only the last profile and omits the other exclusion.

After one parallel story returns a routing stop, cancelled sibling stories are registered as auth cancellations and subsequently stamped as CATEGORY_AUTH InfrastructureAbort with an empty authentication reason.

The scheduler stores the routing stop in a local routing_stop_reason while SprintStopCondition separately owns the terminal reason, allowing story-level skip reasons and the final sprint reason to diverge when stop_if_unset preserves an earlier stop.

The generic zero-spend test in Step 7 does not enumerate tier-dependent exhaustion or intake-remediation spend.
  Suggestion: Specify a pre-spend viability design that runs before intake remediation and batch preflight and can soundly determine every phase pool that the story may select, or revise the routing sequence so exact phase selection is available before the first paid call. Add seam tests for tier-specific exhaustion and intake auto-fix enabled, both asserting $0.00.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Steps 4 and 5 do not account for all callers of _apply_preflight_config(). Besides coordinator/preflight_flow.py, it is called directly from coordinator/engine.py on cache-valid fresh and resume paths. Sprint execution normally obtains batch-preflight state through sprint/collision.py::run_batch_preflight() and later enters those cached paths. Without updating engine.py, a new routing-refusal exception can escape as a generic failure, and later stories can reuse routing resolved during the upfront batch rather than resolving current availability at their actual selection boundary.
  Suggestion: Add src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py and the cached/resume call paths explicitly to Steps 4 and 5. Define how each caller receives a fresh answer and converts pool exhaustion into the same non-failure routing outcome; test both standalone and sprint cached-preflight execution.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 1 (spend ordering) is retired only partially. Step 4 says catch the refusal 'at the coordinator routing boundary and at sprint pre-dispatch where possible' — but by the time assign_models runs, preflight complexity has already been paid, so a refusal raised only there would violate the AC's 'before any spend on that story'. Step 7 asserts zero spend but the plan does not state where the tier-independent precheck lives.
  Suggestion: Make the pre-dispatch precheck role-pool-wide and tier-independent: before any paid phase, resolve availability for every configured candidate of each required role and refuse if a role's whole pool is unavailable. Keep the assignment-time refusal as the exact per-phase enforcement, and have the Step 7 zero-spend test drive the sprint from before preflight, not from assign_models.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 2 (account/auth-mode-scoped availability vs identity-scoped capability exclusions) is retired in shape but the key mapping is unspecified. resolve_model_availability keys its result dict on target.key or target.canonical_id (config/auth.py:~567), while candidate pools and capability_excluded are keyed on AgentDef.name (assignment.py:2101, 2189).
  Suggestion: Fix one explicit key convention in Step 1 (e.g. build targets with key=agent.name for assignment-facing resolution) and assert the mapping in the Step 7 seam test so a same-model-different-credentials pair does not collide or silently miss its exclusion.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 5's per-story resolution can trigger a live account-catalog fetch (_openai_catalog) on every story; the resolver only memoizes catalogs within a single call, so failure/latency behavior across stories is unspecified.
  Suggestion: State that a catalog fetch failure yields unverified (fully eligible, warn once) rather than unavailable, and consider a short-lived per-sprint cache keyed on the dispatch identity tuple that still allows a changed answer to take effect for later stories.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-fable-cli] Plan risk 1 (preflight complexity is itself paid spend) is retired for the whole-phase-empty case by the Step 4 pre-dispatch precheck and Step 7's zero-spend test, but one residual is unaddressed: if tier/exploration selection after paid preflight narrows the pool in a way that only then empties it (e.g. tier-pinned profiles), some preflight spend precedes the stop. The AC reads 'before any spend on that story'.
  Suggestion: Have the pre-dispatch precheck evaluate the union of all tiers' configured candidates per phase — if every configured identity for a phase is unavailable, stop before preflight dispatch; assignment-level enforcement then covers tier-narrowed cases as a best-effort backstop.
- [P2] [anthropic-fable-cli] coordinator/engine.py calls _apply_preflight_config directly at engine.py:1431 and :1861 but is not in any step's file list. If Step 5 changes _apply_preflight_config's signature to accept availability answers, those callers break.

- [P2] [anthropic-fable-cli] Step 1 proposes moving/sharing _availability_target/_availability_targets out of cli/check_config.py; check_config.py builds targets from ForgeConfig including reviewer/fallback keys (lines 431-556), and a move must keep the check-config CLI path working.

finding_registry.description: When a multi-profile explicit review_pool or plan_agent_review contains an unavailable reviewer after an available first entry, the coordinator restores that reviewer into the runtime reviewer list and records it in the routing decision as included: true with reason none.
When a sprint phase has two distinct candidates with the same profile.model and both resolve unavailable, check_sprint_availability collapses them to one excluded entry and returns no stop.

After the singleton availability-warning tracker has warned for an unverified model, a later sprint or task run in the same process does not warn for that model because no run-boundary code resets the tracker.

On the live coordinator path the preflight agent runs and is charged (preflight_flow.py:534) before availability is resolved and routing is applied (preflight_flow.py:1140), so a NoAvailableModelError raised there stops the story after preflight spend while its operator-facing message asserts 'Nothing dispatched, $0.00 spent'.

When a role pool empties from the combination of capability exclusions and availability exclusions, the whole-pool guard raises NoAvailableModelError naming only the availability-excluded agents, so the stop message can attribute the emptiness entirely to account availability while capability records removed the other candidates.

check_sprint_availability keys its excluded map by model name while phase_keys is per profile, so a phase whose candidate list contains two profiles sharing one model name never satisfies the equal-length check and the launch gate silently passes even when every candidate is unavailable, deferring the stop to the router.

AVAILABILITY_WARNINGS is a process-wide singleton with a reset() method that no production code calls, so in a process that runs more than one sprint the once-per-run warning is actually once per process and a later sprint's unverified models are silently unannounced.
When adaptive assignment is disabled, story configuration returns before availability is resolved, so unavailable fixed profiles remain dispatchable and unverified profiles emit no warning.

In adaptive runs the current availability answer is fetched only after the preflight agent call, while the sprint launch check admits preflight when any adaptive agent is available, so an unavailable configured preflight model can incur cost before routing excludes it.
When a per-story routing stop occurs after sprint launch, the sprint records the infrastructure-flagged PREFLIGHT result as FAILED and continues scheduling instead of stopping the run.
When availability and another hard eligibility rule jointly empty a phase, the routing stop names only availability-excluded models and omits every model excluded for the other reason.

When an explicit code-review or plan-review pool has an unavailable first reviewer and an available later reviewer, the sprint availability gate reports the phase as having no available model and aborts launch.

When a non-leading explicit reviewer is dropped for unavailability, the runtime review pool is filtered but the routing decision omits that pinned reviewer or records the matching agent only as explicit_override_locked instead of model_unavailable.
When a fixed-profile phase has two unavailable dispatch identities with the same model string, the per-story routing stop collapses them into one excluded entry and names the model only once.

In the preflight-profile refusal catch, state.error is set to the bare exception text while the returned CoordinatorResult message is built via routing_stop_message with the spend tail, so the persisted state error and the operator-facing message for the same stop carry different sentences.

_fixed_profile_availability keys the warning map by profile.model via setdefault, so two configured phase profiles sharing a model string under different endpoints or transports collapse into one warning entry and only the first identity's unverified or unavailable answer is announced.

The resume-path catch around restore_routing_decision converts a NoAvailableModelError into a RoutingStopped result, but no test drives restore_routing_decision to actually raise on a resumed story whose pool emptied, so that conversion is exercised only by inspection.
With adaptive assignment disabled, a review or plan-review pool containing both an available profile and an unavailable profile returns unchanged, so the unavailable reviewer remains dispatchable.

After an unavailable member is removed from an explicit reviewer pool, the reconciled routing decision omits that profile or labels a matching adaptive agent explicit_override_locked instead of recording model_unavailable with its auth mode and timestamp.
When one unverified dispatch identity appears as a fixed profile and as an agent with a different name, the same run emits separate warnings under the model name and agent name.

After one parallel story returns a routing stop, cancelled sibling stories are registered as auth cancellations and subsequently stamped as CATEGORY_AUTH InfrastructureAbort with an empty authentication reason.

The scheduler stores the routing stop in a local routing_stop_reason while SprintStopCondition separately owns the terminal reason, allowing story-level skip reasons and the final sprint reason to diverge when stop_if_unset preserves an earlier stop.

When an adaptive task pinned the planner to an unavailable profile that was not also present in the adaptive agent pool, routing completed with that planner selected and the PLAN phase would dispatch it instead of producing a routing stop.

In _apply_static_availability, a non-reviewer phase whose candidate list partially survives (preflight with an unavailable primary and available fallback) logs a ROUTING line saying the unavailable model was dropped, but no config replacement is made for that phase — the actual reseat happens later in _availability_checked_preflight_profile, which logs its own line, so the same event can be narrated twice with slightly different wording.

model_availability.py has grown to roughly 723 lines, above the repository's non-blocking 600-line module guideline, mixing target construction, resolution, phase-candidate derivation, rendering, and the warning tracker in one module.

When the configured preflight profile is available but a later phase's candidate pool is entirely unavailable, a live task invokes and charges preflight before returning the routing stop, so the story stops with nonzero spend.

When an adaptive run pins dev or planner to a dispatch identity absent from the agent registry, an unavailable answer for that pin is omitted from the router input and the pinned model remains seated.

Review-only runs, including batch-member reviews, pass the configured review pool to review execution without resolving or filtering current availability, so a known-unavailable reviewer can still be dispatched.

When a multi-reviewer panel has an unavailable synthesis profile, availability resolution includes that target but phase derivation omits synthesis, and review aggregation can still invoke the unavailable model.

A static mixed reviewer pool drops its unavailable member at runtime but leaves the routing decision unset, so the audit records no model_unavailable exclusion, auth mode, or checked time for that member.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
